newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JAGR AGGRAVATES GROIN INJURY, DOUBTFUL ABOUT RETURN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JAGR AGGRAVATES GROIN INJURY, DOUBTFUL ABOUT RETURN.

text.p: Pittsburgh Penguins star right winger Jaromir Jagr, who leads the NHL with 45 goals, aggravated a groin injury in Thursday night's 4-1 loss at Detroit and suggested he could be out for the season.
Jagr returned Thursday night after missing three games with the same injury. He collided with Detroit defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov early in the second period and did not return.
"I felt pretty good until then," Jagr said. "It didn't bother me at all."
Penguins coach Ed Johnston said he hoped the 25-year-old winger could return by mid-March, but Jagr was less optimistic.
"I think it'll be longer," he said. "I don't know, maybe the playoffs, maybe next year."

Jagr is second in the league in secoring, behind teammate Mario Lemieux, with 45 goals and 42 assists in 57 games. Pittsburgh is 21-8-4 when Jagr scores at least one goal and 10-17-1 when he does not.
